headline: Revenue dips y/y as stock-comp timing squeezes margins
summary_short: GCI Liberty's Q1 2026 revenue was $256M (-3.8% y/y, +7.1% q/q) as lost video revenue and a non-repeat 2025 healthcare rate benefit weighed on the top line; operating income fell to $30M and net income to $18M on higher stock comp and Quintillion acquisition costs.
summary_long: Revenue fell 3.8% y/y to $256M as consumer data/other revenue declined (video service discontinued) and a 2025 one-time healthcare rate-appeal benefit didn't repeat, partly offset by consumer-wireless subscriber growth; revenue rose 7.1% q/q. Costs rose on higher technology professional-service fees, Services-Agreement SG&A allocations, a $6M stock-comp increase from delayed 2026 grant timing, and $3M of Quintillion acquisition costs — operating income fell 48% y/y to $30M and Adjusted OIBDA fell to $93M from $113M. Net income dropped to $18M. Cash rose to $435M on the November rights offering; long-term debt eased to $981M; equity grew to $1.71B. No forward guidance was issued this quarter.

drivers.explanation: Consumer data revenue fell on fewer subscribers and consumer other lost video revenue (discontinued in 2025); business data lost a 2025 one-time healthcare rate-appeal benefit, partly offset by consumer wireless subscriber growth.

Higher technology expense (professional-service fees), Services-Agreement SG&A allocations, a stock-comp increase from delayed 2026 grant timing, and new Quintillion acquisition costs outweighed lower consumer/business direct costs.
Direction mirrors operating income — higher technology, SG&A and stock-comp expense plus acquisition costs. The release's own non-GAAP Adjusted OIBDA fell $20M y/y for the same reasons.
Net earnings decline reflects the combined revenue, operating-expense and other-income movements described elsewhere in the release; no additional cause given.
Mirrors the net income decline; diluted weighted-average shares were essentially flat, so per-share earnings tracked the dollar decline in net income.
Decrease driven by lower net earnings and timing differences in working-capital accounts, per the release's liquidity discussion.
Reflects this quarter's net cash flow: $78M from operations less $55M net investing (mostly capex, net of grant proceeds) and $4M of financing outflows.
Growth driven by $18M of net earnings and $8M of stock-based compensation per the equity roll-forward, partly offset by $2M of other equity adjustments.

Board approved renaming the parent to Liberty Capital Corporation (tickers unchanged) and, after quarter-end, agreed to acquire Quintillion for $310M and bought a ~$107M Liberty Latin America equity stake.
